Scales describes an instrument for determining the weight of an object or comparing the weight of two objects. It consists of a central post with a crossbar from which two pans are hung. An object may be placed in one pan and known weights placed in the other pan until the crossbar remains level, indicating that both pans contain an equal weight. Or one object may be placed in one pan and a different object in the other pan; the pan that hangs lower contains the heavier object.

Here, whole stone refers to a stone people use as a standard weight on a pair of Scales that accurately weighs the whole amount that people expect it to weigh. Merchants could deceive and cheat their customers by using a stone that was not the correct weight.

A merchant who sells things by weight would use a scale to determine their value. he would have stones that were of a standard weight to place on one side of the scale, and the article for sale on the other. 29:12: Here, listens attentively implies that this ruler believes what he listens to.
29:14: Solomon uses the phrase to perpetuity here as an overstatement for emphasis.

29:16: Here, increase could refer to: (1) the wicked increasing their influence or authority in society; (2) the number of the wicked increasing.

29:17: Here, Solomon is speaking as if being free from worry were actually resting.

29:18: Here, vision refers specifically to information that the Lord reveals to prophets so that they can tell it to the people. It is also called “prophecy” or “divine revelation”.

29:19: Here, answer refers to the servant responding by obeying.

29:21: Here Solomon implies that youth refers to the youth of the servant.

29:23: Here, low refers to being humiliated or ashamed.

29:25: Here Solomon speaks of someone causing trouble for himself as if his anxiety were a person who sets a snare that traps him.

29:27: Here Solomon uses way to refer to how people behave.
